interest: This document is valuable to diplomatic and military historians studying interwar naval arms limitation and intelligence monitoring of Japanese rearmament during the 1930s. It illustrates the State Department's ongoing vigilance concerning potential Japanese violations of the non-fortification and status quo provisions of the 1922 Washington Naval Treaty in both the Pacific insular territories and the strategic Kuril Islands. In addition, the docket reveals the wide variety of information channels relied upon by American diplomats, ranging from diplomatic inquiries arriving via the American legation in Riga, Latvia, to British military attaché intelligence and internal Far Eastern Affairs analyses of major Japanese naval shipbuilding infrastructure such as Kawasaki Dockyards.
overview: This file comprises a Department of State List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.345, which covers records relating to Japanese equipment and supplies, naval and coaling stations, and the construction, purchase, and repair of vessels between 1932 and 1937. The sheet indexes three archival entries: an August 1932 despatch (No. 652) from U.S. Minister Robert P. Skinner in Latvia regarding an inquiry into whether Japanese fortifications in Pacific insular territories maintained the status quo mandated by the Washington Naval Treaty (cross-referenced to 894.30/75); a July 1934 British Military Attaché report citing London press accounts concerning Japanese naval base construction in the Kuril Islands; and a March 1937 Division of Far Eastern Affairs note (No. 98) by Scott analyzing intelligence and commenting on reports regarding the possible purchase of Kawasaki Dockyards.

subfiles.summary: This sub-file consists of a single-page Department of State List of Papers sheet cataloguing entries 3 through 5 for decimal file 894.345 relating to Japanese naval equipment, stations, and vessel construction. Entry 3 records an August 20, 1932 despatch (No. 652) from Minister Robert P. Skinner in Latvia regarding an inquiry into Japanese fortifications in Pacific insular territories under the Washington Treaty, cross-referenced to 894.30/75. Entry 4 indexes a July 10, 1934 report from the British Military Attaché quoting London press reports on Japanese naval base construction in the Kuril Islands. Entry 5 indexes a March 27, 1937 Division of Far Eastern Affairs note (No. 98) by Scott commenting on reports regarding the possible purchase of Kawasaki Dockyards.
